prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1077; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed rear impact while backing out of a parking space in a retail lot and said they felt neck pain within the hour. The claim was opened and the file assigned for review.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. No concerns were raised on the policy side.

Entry 3: Obtained the other driver's statement, which matches the claimant's description of how the collision happened. Requested photos from both vehicles.

Entry 4: Photos of both vehicles show damage consistent with the impact described. Bumper and tail panel damage lines up with the contact point mentioned by both parties.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone. They repeated the same account of the collision and of who was in the car, and confirmed they had no prior damage to the vehicle that I am aware of.

Entry 6: Police report notes the claimant was present in the vehicle and lists two independent witnesses from the lot. Both witnesses gave statements that match the reported sequence of events.

Entry 7: Claimant sent medical records showing a diagnosis of whiplash and a treatment plan involving physiotherapy. Records do not show any prior neck or upper back complaints.

Entry 8: Checked prior claim history and the claimant's records give no indication of earlier injury to the neck or upper back. Causation of the current symptoms is still not clear and will need medical review.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a usual course, with visits tapering as the claimant reported steady improvement. Next step is a records review to confirm the injury is linked to this collision.

Entry 10: Claim remains open pending the medical review. Claimant has been told what documents are still needed and has agreed to provide them.
